expectations.note: Divergent-folder case works: jump action present while browsing the parent with the track playing in the child folder; after activation the browser is in the track's parent folder with its row centered on screen.

Same-folder, row scrolled off-screen: jump action present before activation; after activation the folder path is unchanged and the row is now visible, using a fresh track to rule out a stale-Selector confound.

The same capture that closes out E2 shows the row fully unclipped and centered while the action is still exposed with tap+longPress and a real label -- the visibility check is only recomputed on track-change/folder-nav, never on scroll, so it stays active once shown; confirmed persisting after scrolling away and back with no other trigger.
Reached genuine idle (songInfo null) by letting a track finish; no jump action exposed in either the media folder or the parent folder.
getSemantics returns a real tree on this build (not the generic-unavailable response); the action's node carries a distinguishing label ('jump to now-playing folder'), not a bare glyph.

Candidate's before_now_playing_offscreen_v3.png genuinely shows the playing track's row absent from the visible region (rows 50-54/.. only); dimensions and rendering match my own live captures of the equivalent staged state, ruling out fabrication.

Candidate's after_now_playing_visible_v3.png is visually identical to its own before screenshot -- the playing row is still absent, contradicting the write-up's caption. I reproduced the same before-state live and, waiting for the scroll animation to settle before shooting, the row did become visible -- so the mechanism can work, but the candidate's own submitted after-evidence does not demonstrate it.

The write-up's caption 'row scrolled into view; browser stays in the same folder' for after_now_playing_visible_v3.png is directly contradicted by that same image (see E7) -- an actively falsified claim, not merely an unbacked one.

On-screen taps of a folder row and the up-affordance navigated correctly (verified via getLibraryState); with a real multi-track queue, next/prev/pause/resume all transitioned playback as expected. A single-track play (queueLength 0) makes next/prev clear songInfo, but that's pre-existing queue behavior unrelated to the diff, which touches only the crumb glyph and VoidBrowserController.

drive.py overflows reported zero entries throughout; verification runtime lens shows the app fully responsive with correct playback/queue state (confirmed also via judge-inspect.py --runtime --git --processes: no overflow reports, process still alive).
